findings.title: Clause headers consume next-statement directives without suppressing any statement
findings.requirement: nosec-next-line must suppress the next statement after the directive, rather than a continuation clause of a statement that already started.
findings.evidence:
Reproduced with real enabled B101/B307 plugins: if True:
    pass
# nosec-next-line B307
else:
    eval("1")
eval("2")
. Both B307 findings remain at lines 5 and 6, and skipped_tests is 0. The same failure occurs with a directive immediately before finally:. The token collector finishes an entry for else: or finally: at NEWLINE; finish() treats that clause header as a new statement and removes the pending directive. Neither header is an independent statement, so the suppression is lost before it reaches an actual target statement. Repair statement classification so continuation-only clause headers do not consume pending next-statement directives; add real-plugin tests for else/finally and related clause boundaries.

findings.title: Single-line compound suites arbitrarily suppress only their first child statement
findings.requirement: Next-statement suppression must have consistent statement boundaries and suppress only its target, rather than changing scope according to whether a compound suite shares a physical line with its header.
findings.evidence:
Reproduced: # nosec-next-line B307
if eval("0"): eval("1"); eval("2")
eval("3")
. The implementation suppresses eval("0") and eval("1"), but reports eval("2") and eval("3"); skipped_tests is 2. Putting the same suite on the next indented line suppresses only eval("0") and reports both body calls; skipped_tests becomes 1. The collector splits on semicolons/NEWLINE but never separates a compound header from its same-line suite, so the first body statement is accidentally merged with the header. This contradicts the implementation's explicit header-only behavior tested by test_next_line_does_not_suppress_whole_suite, and even a whole-compound-statement interpretation would require suppressing both body calls, not just one. Repair header/simple-suite boundaries while preserving legitimate colons in expressions, and cover one-line if/def/other suites and semicolon-separated children with regression tests.

findings.title: Preserve physical-region suppression for findings on comment-only lines
findings.requirement: A nosec-begin region suppresses findings on subsequent physical lines until nosec-end; selector resolution and metrics must apply to all enabled tests, including file-level tests.
findings.evidence:
Reproduced with real BanditManager and enabled tests B101,B613: source '# nosec-begin B613
# ‮
# nosec-end
assert True
' still reports B613 at line 2, with skipped_tests=0. Expected only B101 at line 4 and skipped_tests=1. An equivalent legacy inline comment '# ‮ # nosec B613' correctly suppresses B613, confirming the existing public interface supports this finding location. build_suppressions computes physical[2], but discards physical coverage after constructing entries for tokenized statements. A comment-only line outside a statement has no entry, so for_result returns no suppression. Retain physical-region coverage in SuppressionMap and combine it at a finding's reported line, including when no statement contains that line. Add real-plugin tests for comment-only coverage and begin/end boundaries.

findings.title: Do not apply next-statement suppression to other statements sharing the reported line
findings.requirement: nosec-next-line suppresses only the next statement, and applicable suppressions must be determined for the finding rather than unrelated statements.
findings.evidence:
With enabled tests B101,B613, source '# nosec-next-line B613
x = 1; y = "‮"
assert True
' incorrectly suppresses the B613 finding in the second assignment and increments skipped_tests to 1. Without the directive, B613 is reported at the second assignment's line/column. The first assignment is the directive's target and contains no bidi character, so B613 in the second assignment must remain. for_result unions suppressions from every statement on result.lineno, ignoring the stored start/end columns and result.col_offset. This lets a directive on a harmless statement hide a security finding in an unrelated statement. Resolve the reported finding to its containing statement using the reported position, taking account of the plugin's column convention, rather than unioning every statement on the line. Add a regression paired with a bidi character in the first assignment to verify both positive and negative targeting.
